mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% compresses corporate profit margins through higher borrowing costs and increases the discount rate for equity valuation, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 205.0 signals persistent inflation that triggers Fed rate-holding behavior, reducing equity attractiveness and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 205.0 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate above 4.0% indicates economic weakness that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and UNRATE < 4.6% signals monetary tightening with labor market strength, increasing corporate cost pressures and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with labor strength
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS > 5.0 AND UNRATE < 4.6) fails when SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of such instances (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1500 (HOUST > 1500) indicate robust consumer demand for housing, accelerating retail and construction sector growth and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1500 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 110.0 (INDPRO > 110.0) signals manufacturing expansion that increases corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when INDPRO > 110.0 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: GDP level above 11500 (GDPC1 > 11500) indicates late-cycle expansion where overvaluation and rising input costs reduce equity returns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 > 11500 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous PAYEMS > 137000 and UNRATE < 4.6% signals a tight labor market with rising wage pressures, increasing corporate costs and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS > 137000 AND UNRATE < 4.6%) fails when SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of such instances (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
